candidate_relations.reason: WPW syndrome implies tachyarrhythmia; the record shows a WPW pattern (delta wave, short PR) without documented SVT, and it also omits the heart-failure exacerbation.
There is no imaging or history supporting chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
Global hypokinesis with EF <25% is attributed to known cardiomyopathy, not acute myocarditis.
HFrEF captures the heart-failure component but omits the WPW pattern.
No pulsus paradoxus, pericardial knock, or constriction physiology is described.
Dilated/global hypokinetic cardiomyopathy describes the ventricular phenotype but omits WPW and the acute HF exacerbation framing.
Scrotal and leg edema are congestion signs of the HF exacerbation, not the composite diagnosis.
Polysubstance-related cardiomyopathy explains the low EF but omits the WPW pattern and the exacerbation event.
Dependent scrotal/leg swelling in decompensated HFrEF is not primary lymphedema.
WPW pattern matches the ECG component but omits the required heart-failure exacerbation.

case_quality_flags: Reference is a composite of WPW pattern plus heart-failure exacerbation; no candidate contains both.
